title: AgentLoop Governance Fail-Open Inventory and Orchestration Split
summary: Audit date: 2026-05-20. Documents the current governance fail-open seams and the minimum orchestration split needed to patch them safely.

sections.content: AgentLoop Governance Fail-Open Inventory and Orchestration Split

Audit date: 2026-05-20. This document captures the governance paths that currently fail open, the graceful-degradation behavior each one should use instead, and the orchestration split needed to keep AgentLoop from absorbing more policy and tracing logic.

rows: Exceptions in `permission_decision()` and `approval_request()` return allow; patch-gate lookup failures return `None`, which lets mutation continue.
Return typed refusals such as `permission_unavailable`, `approval_unavailable`, or `patch_gate_unavailable`; keep read-only tools available, but never convert a gate failure into allow.
Capability-gate failures, single-provider short-circuits, and council consultation exceptions all map to `ALLOW`.
Return `BLOCK` or `REVIEW` with `council_unavailable`; mutation tools should pause for manual review or no-op instead of continuing silently.
`git status` failures are swallowed, `_captured` is set, and init uses `WARN_ALLOW` for non-subagent sessions.
Record `dirty_guard_capture_failed`, block mutation tools, and leave read-only inspection available until the guard can be recaptured.
The default policy allows dev bypass, and checkpoint auto-mints a dev receipt when none is provided.
Require an explicit dev-mode policy flag; otherwise refuse missing receipts with a clear authorization failure and no implicit minting.
Bare `ToolRuntime` defaults permission, approval, and patch gating to allow/none.
Require an explicit governance policy object or default to fail-closed for mutation when the policy callbacks are absent.
The runtime execution runner creates `ToolRuntime` without permission/approval/patch-gate callbacks; adapter policy hints are metadata only.
Pass a policy object through the runner and refuse mutation dispatch if the policy is missing or incomplete.
Missing coordination state returns `False`, and the tool continues instead of treating the missing lease context as a blocker.
If a mutation cannot establish coordination, fall back to an explicit dry-run/read-only refusal unless the caller opted into a non-coordinated mode.
Missing coordination store or compile failure returns empty packets or `safe_paths=requesting_paths` with `overall_risk="none"`.
Emit `overall_risk="unknown"`, do not report safe paths when evidence is missing, and require manual review before downstream mutation guidance is trusted.

items: Mutation gate failures resolve to `BLOCK`, `REVIEW`, or `DEGRADED`, never `ALLOW`.
Read-only tools may continue when the only problem is governance availability.
Missing evidence must surface as `unknown`, not `none`.
Dev bypass is only acceptable when it is explicitly enabled and labeled in the policy path and receipt path.
Policy hints remain advisory until a policy object is injected into the executor.
Coordination failure should produce a dry-run or refusal, not an unleased write.

rows: Turn/session topology, message pump, model turn sequencing, lifecycle cleanup
The loop itself should remain thin, but policy decisions should not accumulate here.
Keeps the compatibility shell focused on orchestration instead of governance mechanics.
Dirty guard, permission, approval, council consult, patch gate, typed fallback decisions
All branchy policy classification and failure handling.
Centralizes fail-open prevention and makes degraded outcomes explicit and testable.
ToolRuntime wiring, governed tool invocation, result normalization, receipts
The executor should not decide policy defaults by itself.
Keeps execution authority inside the runtime boundary while preserving a single policy object.
Context build, collision/handoff packet degradation, context evidence shaping
Lets missing evidence become an explicit degraded packet instead of a fabricated safe packet.
Correlation keys and hashes that span turns, tools, leases, receipts, and refusals
Ad hoc propagation through closure arguments and local temp variables.
Improves correlated tracing and makes failure chains debuggable across the whole stack.
Joins turn history, dirty-guard state, coordination state, and receipts.
AgentLoop, dirty guard, runtime requests, evidence emitters
Separates each orchestration iteration and its downstream tool batch.
Correlates the request, execution result, refusal, and receipt for one tool action.
Binds the tool request payload to the execution and evidence chain.
Lets degraded or refused operations still be traced without raw payload leakage.
Connects mutation checks to the dirty-file snapshot that existed at mission start.
Binds leases and coordination reservations to a specific mutation attempt.
Coordination store, write tools, runtime lease claims

items: Convert the fail-open branches to typed degraded refusals before adding any new orchestration split.
Make `ToolRuntime` require an explicit policy object or fail closed when the policy is missing.
Thread the policy object through the runtime execution runner so metadata hints are enforced, not just recorded.
Extract governance decisions out of `AgentLoop` into a dedicated governance boundary.
Add tests for the fail-open, degraded, and trace-propagation paths before renaming or flattening the shell.

rows: Each gate failure returns a typed refusal or degraded outcome instead of `ALLOW`.
`ToolRuntime` refuses mutation when no policy object is injected.
Missing coordination context produces dry-run or refusal behavior, not an unleased write.
Missing evidence yields `unknown` risk and no fabricated safe paths.
The correlation keys survive degraded and refusal paths.
The new audit document validates against `rig.documentation.page.v1`.

disclosure.progressive_summary: Audit the AgentLoop governance fail-open seams, list the typed degraded outcomes each one should use instead, and separate orchestration, governance, execution, context assembly, and trace propagation into narrower modules.
